title: Galgano Borghesi to Leonardo Benvoglienti, Naples, 12 May 1456 (ASSi Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 4, DECODE R4793)

steps.what: Found the whole busta Concistoro 2308 on DECODE (keys R4746-R4789, letters R4790-R4814, R1858), missed by the 23 Sept scan; downloaded 131 images with the project cookie (the session that worked on all the Concistoro letters).

Senatore 2009 (Callisto III nelle corrispondenze diplomatiche, Revista Borja 2) cites 'una lettera in cifra di Borghesi a Benvoglienti ... Concistoro 2308, c. 4 (da Napoli, 12 maggio [1456])' and lists Concistoro 2308 as 'lettere cifrate e cifrari di ambasciatori'; no decipherment printed. Treccani DBI Borghese: none.

Compared by eye the alphabets of the 1450s keys R4750 (Milan ambassadors 1454, same Latin code-word family: 'storpsi' = ambasciatore fiorentino), R4753, R4754, R4756, R4762 with the signs of no. 4 (1456): none produces its letters.

No. 4: six 1450s keys of fasc. 1 transcribed (keys/R47xx.txt); none gives the letter's values. A two-row alphabet fragment written below the letter's text (i-u) plus the recipient's interlinear glosses rebuild the key: 114/144 sign tokens read (79%), 125 with context.
Split on 14 Oct 2026 from siena1421 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): each letter of the bundle has its own key; this entry is no. 4 only.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcripts/no04.txt + transcripts/no04_reading.txt; key keys/no04_key.txt

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): transcripts/no04_reading.txt read through with its running text. The first cipher runs complete their clear sentences, but the second paragraph is runs, code words and '?' signs between doubtful clear words and cannot be built into sentences; the page gives the sense as tentative. Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> not solved; fraction_read 0.79 -> 0.

Re-read brief b25: DECODE R4793 re-fetched (two images, no attachment); ll. 17-24 and their interlinear glosses re-read on per-line crops. Gloss over pedesi = 'Iacopino' (was 'sa? piu'), over cras = 'a pace'/'pace' (was 'parte'), over toffe = 'al papa'; l. 17 '4 longs' = EL before Calor. Code words cras = pace, pedesi = Iacopino adopted (both cras glosses agree).

Partial reading of the whole letter written (transcripts/no04_reading.md, no04_en.md, log no04_reread_log.md). b17_score.py LANG_=it on the body: 0.594 (19/32), explicit holes 0.719; before: no reading body. Reader's test fails for the second paragraph (only its first sentence holds); stays decoded, not read.

Consistency pass (cl): outcome.texts summary reworded for docs/_check_terms.py (outcome words 'read', 'undeciphered', 'unsolved' replaced by what happened: deciphered, given a value, transcribed, no decipherment known); facts unchanged.

validation.notes: 144 cipher signs in 15 short runs, most of them a few letters long, with 9 Latin code words: too few read tokens per sign type for the shuffled-text test, and the key is attested by the alphabet fragment written on the letter

texts.label: Naples, 12 May 1456, ASSi Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 4 (DECODE R4793)
texts.summary: Galgano Borghesi, orator at Naples, writes to Leonardo Benvoglienti that at his urging King Alfonso wanted the settlement to include the promises made when Lucca was besieged by the Florentines, and that the Pope, the Florentine clergy and the cardinals are to contribute against the Turk. The sense is tentative: 114 of the 144 cipher signs are given a value.

prior.where: the recipient's interlinear glosses over some runs, and an alphabet fragment below the text
